name: Single-tuned harmonic filter
summary: A shunt series-LC branch tuned near one harmonic order to sink that harmonic current from the network.
description: A single-tuned filter is a capacitor and reactor in series, connected in shunt and tuned to resonate near one harmonic frequency, often slightly below the 5th, 7th or 11th. At that frequency it presents a low impedance and draws harmonic current away from the network, while at fundamental frequency it supplies capacitive reactive power.

Drawings show a capacitor and reactor in series on a shunt branch, labelled with the tuned order, and often several such branches for different orders. Unbalance protection for the capacitor bank and a dedicated breaker are normally shown.

A tuned filter creates a parallel resonance with the network at a frequency just below its tuning, which can amplify other harmonics. The symbol does not show the network impedance scan or detuning tolerance, so the harmonic study must accompany it.
readingNotes: Read the harmonic order label on each branch.
The filter also supplies fundamental reactive power.
drawingChecklist: State tuned order, Mvar and quality factor.
distinction: A single-tuned filter targets one harmonic order; a damped high-pass filter attenuates a broad band above its corner frequency.
